title: Design Patterns for Python Enterprise (PYTH_166_S1 to PYTH_166_S8)

slides.title: Enterprise Design Patterns
slides.prompt: Applying battle-tested patterns like Factory, Strategy, and Decorator improves maintainability and extensibility.

slides.title: Factory Pattern Implementation
slides.prompt: Fill in the pattern name used to encapsulate object creation logic based on runtime inputs.

slides.title: Singleton Pattern Pitfalls
slides.prompt: Why is the Singleton pattern often considered an anti-pattern in modern unit-tested Python applications?
options: It introduces global state, making isolation and unit testing difficult
It increases Python memory consumption by 50%
It prevents functions from accepting arguments
It breaks compatibility with Linux operating systems
slides.correctAnswer: It introduces global state, making isolation and unit testing difficult

slides.title: Strategy Pattern Swapping
slides.prompt: Fill in the pattern type that allows swapping algorithms at runtime via composition.

slides.title: Adapter Pattern Purpose
slides.prompt: When should you implement the Adapter design pattern?
options: To allow incompatible interfaces to work together by wrapping an existing class
To execute tasks across multiple background threads
To cache database query results in RAM
slides.correctAnswer: To allow incompatible interfaces to work together by wrapping an existing class

slides.title: Decorator Pattern Dynamic Wrapping
slides.prompt: Fill in the Python syntax decorator wrapper used to preserve original function signatures.

slides.title: Observer Pattern Mechanics
slides.prompt: How does the Observer design pattern facilitate loose coupling between components?
options: Subject objects notify a list of registered observer objects automatically upon state changes
It forces all classes to inherit from a single base class
It stores all objects inside a single global dictionary
It prevents functions from raising runtime exceptions
slides.correctAnswer: Subject objects notify a list of registered observer objects automatically upon state changes
